categories.main_business_segments: AT&T operates two primary reportable segments: Communications and Latin America. The Communications segment, which accounts for about 97% of revenues, includes Mobility (wireless services and equipment), Business Wireline (fiber, IP voice, managed services, and legacy telecom for businesses), and Consumer Wireline (broadband, fiber, and legacy voice for consumers). The Latin America segment provides wireless services and equipment in Mexico.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: AT&T's core technologies include nationwide 5G and 4G LTE wireless networks, extensive fiber-optic infrastructure, and software-defined networking (SDN) and network function virtualization (NFV) for efficient, scalable service delivery. The company is investing in Open RAN technology to create a more agile, programmable wireless network and leverages integrated platforms for both wired and wireless connectivity.
categories.primary_customers_markets: AT&T serves a broad range of customers including U.S. consumers, multinational corporations, small and mid-sized businesses, government entities, and wholesale customers. Its end markets span wireless and broadband connectivity, with a focus on both consumer and enterprise communications needs, as well as public safety through FirstNet.
categories.geographic_coverage: AT&T's primary operations are in the United States, with nationwide wireless and broadband coverage, and a significant presence in Mexico through its Latin America segment. The company’s U.S. network covers all major metropolitan areas and over 334 million people with LTE and over 302 million with 5G. In Mexico, AT&T serves over 22 million wireless subscribers.
categories.supply_chain_position: AT&T operates as a downstream service provider, delivering end-user connectivity and communications services. It relies on upstream suppliers for network equipment, devices, and technology, and manages a large-scale distribution and retail network for device and service sales.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: AT&T's strategic focus is on expanding its 5G and fiber networks, driving convergence between wireless and wireline services, and deploying Open RAN to foster a more robust, cost-efficient network ecosystem. R&D efforts are concentrated on network design, cybersecurity, advanced IP networking, and leveraging AI for operational efficiencies and customer support.
categories.revenue_model: AT&T generates revenue primarily through recurring service fees for wireless, broadband, and business connectivity, as well as equipment sales (devices and customer premises equipment). Additional revenue streams include managed services, wholesale network access, and, in Mexico, both prepaid and postpaid wireless services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: AT&T faces intense competition from other national wireless carriers (notably Verizon and T-Mobile), regional providers, cable companies, and internet-based service providers. In Mexico, América Móvil is the dominant competitor. AT&T positions itself as a leader in connectivity, emphasizing network quality, integrated offerings, and broad coverage.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, AT&T reported $122.4 billion in operating revenues and $23.5 billion in operating income, with the Communications segment contributing the vast majority. The company has a large asset base ($407 billion in total assets) and serves over 241 million wireless subscribers in the U.S. and 22 million in Mexico. Growth is driven by wireless and fiber broadband, while legacy wireline services continue to decline.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: AT&T differentiates itself through its extensive 5G and fiber networks, integrated wireless and broadband solutions, and a focus on reliability, speed, and coverage. The company emphasizes its ability to deliver seamless connectivity across devices and locations, leadership in public safety communications (FirstNet), and ongoing investment in next-generation network technologies.
